cards.text: Quick catch-up, friend: Paul, the apostle, is a prisoner in Caesarea, and Festus, the Roman governor who took over from Felix, has already heard his case (Acts 24:27; 25:6-12). Several days later, two visitors come down to Caesarea: King Agrippa, and Bernice, who comes with him. A KING, in the building.

cards.question: Why do King Agrippa and Bernice come down to Caesarea?

answers.text: To pay their respects to Festus
To collect taxes from the city
To celebrate a feast in the city

cards.text: They're staying several days, so Festus lays out Paul's case for the king: a man Felix left in prison. Several days? That's not a visit, that's a HOUSEGUEST situation.
Festus says that while he was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews laid out their case against this man. They wanted a judgment against him.

cards.question: Festus told them it's not the Roman custom to hand a man over before he can face his ___ and ___ himself against their charges.
Back in Caesarea, Festus waited a few weeks before hearing Paul's case.
Festus says that when Paul's accusers rose to speak, they charged him with the crimes he had expected.

cards.text: Festus walked in ready for a CRIME. Instead, he gets arguments about their own religion and 'a certain Jesus who had died…'

cards.question: Festus says the arguments were about a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul said was ___.
Festus tells Agrippa why he asked Paul about going to Jerusalem to be tried there. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He was at a loss how to investigate
He was afraid of a riot in Caesarea
He had to report to Jerusalem anyway

cards.question: When Paul appealed, Festus says he ordered Paul held until he could send him to ___.
After Festus lays out Paul's case, King Agrippa tells Festus he would like to hear Paul himself.
Festus declares that Agrippa will hear Paul tomorrow. How do Agrippa and Bernice enter the auditorium the next day?

cards.text: In they come, along with the commanders and the city's leading men, and Festus orders Paul brought in. Back when I was stuck in the back of a junk drawer, the only grand entrance I ever saw was somebody yanking it open to grab a RUBBER BAND.

cards.question: Festus tells the room the whole Jewish community has petitioned him about Paul, both in Caesarea and in Jerusalem. What were they crying out?

answers.text: That he ought not to live any longer
That he should be sent to Rome
That he should be whipped and released

cards.question: Festus tells the crowd he found Paul had done nothing worthy of death.
Festus says he has plenty of definite charges to write to the Emperor about Paul.

cards.text: So Festus has brought Paul before all of them, and especially before King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry he'll have something to write. He is trying HARD not to ship a prisoner to the Emperor with a note that says, 'No idea. Good luck.'

cards.question: Festus says it seems unreasonable to send on a prisoner without specifying the ___ against him.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend, because King Agrippa hasn't heard one word from Paul yet.
